incident.incidentSpecificLocation: East gen pad, near the lime mixing station
incident.detailedIncidentDescription: While repositioning a water pull hose near the lime mixing station, the injured party stepped backward onto an uneven section of graded fill and rolled his right ankle. He was able to bear weight briefly before reporting pain and swelling. Two coworkers assisted him to the site trailer, where first aid was administered and the ankle was wrapped and elevated. Work in the immediate area was paused for approximately twenty minutes while the ground was inspected and marked. No other workers were in the immediate vicinity at the time of the incident.
incident.injuryRemarks: Ice and wrap applied. Employee was advised to see UMMC/AFCU if swelling does not improve by next shift.

witnesses.name: Kris Taute
witnesses.statement: I was operating the water truck about 40 feet away and saw Marcus step back and go down onto one knee. I turned off the truck and went to check on him right away.

witnesses.name: Jake Lytle
witnesses.statement: I helped walk Marcus to the trailer and got the first aid kit. The ground in that area had a hidden dip that wasn't obvious until you were right on top of it.

witnesses.name: Delores Fenwick
witnesses.statement: I was in the area for a site walk and saw the crew respond quickly and professionally.

incident.natureOfDamage: Coupling cracked when dropped during the incident
incident.supervisorNotes: Area has been flagged and will be re-graded before work resumes. Toolbox talk held with crew on inspecting footing before backing/repositioning hoses and equipment near graded fill.
incident.safetyConsultantNotes: Recommend adding a daily ground-condition check to the JSA for lime mixing operations and marking soft/uneven fill areas with cones until regraded.

disciplinary.whatOccurred: Employee operated the excavator without a spotter present near an active utility trench, in violation of the site traffic control plan.
disciplinary.earlierWarnings: Verbal warning given on 2026-06-14 for a similar spotter-related concern.
disciplinary.companyPolicyStates: All heavy equipment operation near excavations must use a dedicated spotter per the Shackelford Safety Manual, Section on Heavy Equipment.
disciplinary.employeeStatement: Employee stated the spotter had stepped away briefly and he did not stop work to wait for them to return.
disciplinary.correctiveActionRequired: Employee must stop and wait for a spotter to be present before resuming excavation-adjacent equipment work, every time, no exceptions.
disciplinary.companyWill: The company will retrain the employee on spotter requirements and monitor compliance for the next 30 days.
disciplinary.ifNotCorrected: Continued violations will result in further disciplinary action up to and including termination.

separation.detailedExplanation: Third documented safety violation within a 90-day period (operating equipment without a spotter near an excavation), following the progressive discipline steps already on file (verbal warning, written warning).
separation.rehireReasonIfNo: Repeated safety-critical violations after progressive discipline.

medicalEvent.reportedSymptoms: Employee reported eye irritation and burning after a hydraulic fluid line sprayed near her face while working on the excavator.
medicalEvent.workEventDescription: A hydraulic hose fitting failed while employee was inspecting the excavator boom, spraying fluid toward her face and upper body.
medicalEvent.safetyObservations: Eyes flushed at the on-site eyewash station for 15 minutes per SDS guidance. Employee transported to urgent care for evaluation as a precaution.

uncontrolledEvent.estimatedCost: Approximately $850 in absorbent materials and disposal
uncontrolledEvent.whatHappened: A hydraulic hose on the excavator ruptured during operation, releasing an estimated three gallons of hydraulic fluid onto gravel yard surface. Spill was contained within the yard, away from any drainage.
uncontrolledEvent.immediateActionsTaken: Equipment shut down immediately. Spill kit deployed, absorbent applied, contaminated gravel bagged for disposal. Environmental notified per site plan.
